limitations: Native macOS Apple Silicon/Intel, Windows, and real MCP/broker host integration NOT_RUN; Linux x86_64 alone is runtime-proven.
Caller must validateSession(session, current_boot) before using a static Authorizer; snapshot root/GitMetadata are borrowed until exclusive Registry.deinit.

Only trusted launcher may call registerWorkspace, bindSession, or setManagedWrite. The manifest external workspace label must be approved by launcher and mapped to the newly issued runtime WorkspaceId; I08/I09 signatures have no persisted manifest-label field.

I09 cannot receive SessionContext or OutOfScope in its frozen signature. It requires a prior exact trusted binding and maps scope mismatch to FenceMismatch; dispatcher must check its bound transport session first.

Retired registry entries retain handles and callback counters until exclusive teardown; capacity defaults/hard-caps at32 lifetime incarnations, 16 current sessions,2 concurrent discoveries,64 callbacks per workspace. After capacity exhaustion the host must drain and create a fresh registry.
Git discovery only accepts explicit Git workspace roots; non-Git directories, subdirectory roots, bare repositories, and path spellings containing newline/NUL are refused.
Generation advances on markChanged, changed discovered HEAD, and CommitGuard.markApplied. Watcher integration must call markChanged for dirty file changes; this module does not watch files.
Registry policy snapshots cannot be replaced in place: a different policy or same digest with different contents is rejected. Host rebind uses a fresh registry after drain.

Use acquireCommit(ticket), filesystem publication, markApplied(), release(), then endCallback(ticket). While a guard is held, invoke no ordinary same-workspace Registry methods (including snapshot/validateWorkspace); use the retained Snapshot and guard.next_generation. Owner endCallback returns Busy. Duplicate release is harmless. Guard and callbacks require a stable Registry address and live retained handles.

The publication latch orders participating host operations, not hostile same-UID external filesystem writers. Managed-write approval remains an operational host condition; the editor supplies filesystem CAS and recovery.

Publication waits are bounded to64 per workspace and release the global mutex. After guard acquisition, expiry or revocation waits for release; no old-fence commit may follow successful revocation. Abort does not publish the reserved generation; markApplied is idempotent.
remaining_gates: Native macOS/Windows and actual host integration NOT_RUN

changes: Sample monotonic and wall clocks inside the final serialized authority check after acquiring the registry mutex in all seven affected operations.
Scope disconnect/expired-task revocation to the actual active lease task; keep workspace retirement and explicit revoke workspace-wide.
regressions: Seven deterministic tests block the actual authority mutex, advance injected std.Io clocks across expiry, and verify acquire, renew, lease validation, callback start/commit, bind, and session validation reject.

Two tasks share one workspace: unrelated disconnect, expired acquire, and expired stale lease validate/renew/callback-start preserve the healthy writer; owner disconnect/expiry revoke and drain correctly.

commit_coordinator.red_summary: 38/51 isolation pass; thirteen assertion failures show twelve mutation/expiry/retirement operations complete while a commit guard is held and owner callback completion is not rejected. Guard reservation scaffold exists without lifecycle integration at this RED commit.
commit_coordinator.design: Per-workspace publishing slot and bounded condition waiters release registry mutex during filesystem work; all revoking/expiring/retiring/generation mutation paths wait, then revalidate filesystem identity or relookup bindings as appropriate. Guard ID is monotonic and registry-wide; stored reservation defeats duplicate/stale releases or modified next_generation.
commit_coordinator.consumer_contract: Retain snapshot before acquiring guard. acquireCommit(ticket); publish filesystem; markApplied(); release(); endCallback(ticket). Release without markApplied on abort. No ordinary same-workspace Registry calls while guarded. T11 confirms compliance.
